entries.title: CFTC interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling products from the swap definition publishes at 91 FR 65969, effective October 19, 2026, comments due November 18, 2026
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission interim final rule under RIN 3038-AF81 published in the Federal Register on October 19, 2026 at 91 FR 65969 as document 2026-21376. The document's DATES section states "Effective Date: This interim final rule is effective October 19, 2026" and "Request for comment: Comments must be received by November 18, 2026." The SUMMARY states that the Commission "is adopting an interim final rule" to codify its longstanding position that casino-style gambling products, including wagers placed on sportsbooks and casino games, are excluded from the "swap" definition. The action is recorded as "Interim final rule; request for comments." The document runs from page 65969 to page 65979 of volume 91. When this rule was filed for public inspection on October 16, 2026, its text carried unfilled brackets in place of both dates; the dates above are taken from the published document.
entries.source_label: Federal Register, 91 FR 65969, document 2026-21376 (CFTC interim final rule, RIN 3038-AF81)
entries.relevant_to: sportsbooks, casino operators, prediction-market platforms, derivatives exchanges, futures commission merchants

entries.title: CFTC proposal to define event contracts as swaps publishes at 91 FR 66022, comments due November 18, 2026
entries.facts: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission notice of proposed rulemaking under RIN 3038-AF82 published in the Federal Register on October 19, 2026 at 91 FR 66022 as document 2026-21377. The document's DATES section states "Comments must be received by November 18, 2026." The proposal would further define "swap" to expressly cover event contracts, including contracts on sports, politics, cultural events and weather. The document carries no effective date because it is a proposal, and the action is recorded as "Notice of proposed rulemaking." The document runs from page 66022 to page 66033 of volume 91. This proposal and the interim final rule published the same day at 91 FR 65969 are separate documents with separate legal status: the interim final rule is adopted and excludes casino-style gambling products from the swap definition, while this document is a proposal only and would include event contracts.
entries.source_label: Federal Register, 91 FR 66022, document 2026-21377 (CFTC notice of proposed rulemaking, RIN 3038-AF82)
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, derivatives exchanges, sportsbooks, brokerages offering event contracts

entries.title: Pennsylvania State Police begin skill games enforcement, with seizure and prosecution exposure live as of October 14, 2026
entries.facts: In a release dated October 14, 2026, the Pennsylvania State Police announced that enforcement of the state's skill games law began that day, following the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania's June 15, 2026 ruling that skill games are "slot machines" under the Gaming Act and the expiration of the deadline for businesses to remove unauthorized devices. The release states that devices located outside facilities licensed by the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board are unlawful, and that establishments may face prosecution and immediate seizure as of October 14, 2026. It cites Section 5513 of the Crimes Code as to distributors and manufacturers who maintain, make, sell or lease slot machines without Gaming Control Board authorization. The release states that turning off, unplugging or temporarily disabling a machine does not stop it from being a slot machine. It states that the State Police have reached agreements with six skill games operators or distributors, with agreements with several other distributors pending, under which devices are rendered inoperable from October 14, 2026 and removed on a timeline with inventory and weekly reporting. The release does not state how many devices or establishments are affected, and does not name any operator or distributor.
entries.source_label: Pennsylvania State Police news release, October 14, 2026
entries.relevant_to: skill games operators and distributors, licensed casino operators, bars and retail establishments hosting gaming devices, gaming equipment manufacturers
